home.getText: AI tarot readings for your own cards, on iPhone and Android.

free.a: Yes, to start. You get a free Card of the Day and free AI readings with up to three cards every day once you sign in. Premium adds more.

account.a: Only for AI readings. You can draw cards and look up meanings without one. For AI readings, sign in with Google or Apple, so there is no new password to create.

deck.q: Do I need my own tarot deck?
deck.a: No. You can scan your own Rider-Waite-Smith deck with the camera, or draw cards on screen from the full 78-card deck.

photo.q: Is the photo of my cards uploaded?
photo.a: No. Cards are recognised on your phone and the photo is never saved or sent. Only the card names and your question are used to write the reading.

how.q: How does the AI tarot reading work?
how.a: ShenTarot picks a spread for your question, then writes a reading from the cards you drew, their positions and whether they are upright or reversed. You can ask a follow-up about it.

predict.a: ShenTarot is for entertainment and self-reflection. Readings help you think through a question; they are not predictions or professional advice.

yesNo.title: Yes or No tarot: free three-card reading · ShenTarot
yesNo.description: Ask a yes or no question and draw three tarot cards. Upright cards lean yes, reversed lean no, and the middle card counts double. Free, in your browser.
yesNo.lead: Hold a clear yes or no question in mind and draw three cards. Upright cards lean yes, reversed cards lean no, and the middle card counts double. Each card comes up reversed half the time, so neither answer is favoured.
yesNo.howTitle: How to ask a good yes or no question
yesNo.how1: Ask about one thing, and about something you can act on: "Should I apply for the design job?" works better than "Will my life get better?"
yesNo.how2: Ask once. Drawing again for the same question just adds noise.
yesNo.how3: Read the three meanings, not only the lean. They show what could tip the answer the other way.
yesNo.note: For entertainment and self-reflection. For health, money or legal questions, talk to a professional. See also the {link}.

pairing.twoMajors: Two Major Arcana: one big theme seen from two sides. Ask what {a} and {b} have in common, and where they pull apart.
pairing.majorTheme: {major} sets the theme; {minor} shows where it plays out day to day.
pairing.sameSuit: Both are {suit}: the whole question sits in {sense}.
pairing.sameNumber: Both are {word}: the same stage of a story is showing up in two parts of life.
pairing.neighbours: They sit next to each other in the Major Arcana, so one may be the step that leads to the other.
pairing.twoSameRank: Two {rank}: two people, or two sides of you, acting in a similar way.
pairing.twoCourts: Two court cards: often two people in the situation, or two ways you could act.
pairing.oneCourt: {name} often stands for a person, or a way of acting, in the situation the other card describes.
pairing.bothReversed: Both reversed: the energy of both cards is blocked, delayed or turned inward. Ask what is holding it back.
pairing.oneReversed: {name} is reversed: one part flows while the other is blocked or turned inward.

rel.same: share an element, so they strengthen each other
rel.friendly: have friendly elements, so they support each other
rel.contrary: have opposite elements, so they weaken each other
rel.neutral: neither help nor hinder each other, because one has no single element

pairing.muchWeak: {name} is much weakened: both neighbours oppose it. Read it lightly, as a smaller influence.
pairing.mixed: {name} is mixed: one neighbour supports it and one opposes it.
pairing.someWeak: {name} is somewhat weakened by one opposing neighbour.
pairing.strong: {name} is strengthened: both neighbours support it. Read it as a strong influence.
pairing.someStrong: {name} is somewhat strengthened by one supporting neighbour.
pairing.neither: {name} is neither helped nor hindered by its neighbours.
pairing.bridge: {l} and {r} oppose each other, but {m} gets on with both: it can bridge the two.
